newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 to seesaw in next months but trend still up.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 to seesaw in next months but trend still up.

text.p: Brussels' Bel-20 index won more than one and a half percent on Tuesday on the back of mild U.S. inflation data, but would seesaw in the next few months before heading higher later in the year, analysts said.
"The market will continue to fluctuate -- today it moved up, maybe it will go down in the next few days -- but basically the trend is flat for now," said Stefan Casteleyn at Corluy & Co.
He noted the growing volatility was normal after markets came out of a bull period.
He reiterated an earlier forecast that the Bel-20 would end the year at around 2,300 points.

The Bel-20, lifted in the morning by Monday's 60-point jump on Wall Street and bond and dollar strength, got another boost at 1230 GMT from tame U.S. CPI data which eased inflation and rate hike fears.
"I still believe that European bourses are not expensive... the danger comes from the U.S. One day it's 'yes inflation', the next day it's 'no inflation'. Today, it's 'no inflation'," Casteleyn said.
The dollar, low interest rates and solid company earnings would further support European markets. The rise later in the year would be fuelled by fresh dollar gains, he added.
"There are no big statements that the dollar will rise, which is good. It will rise quietly," Casteleyn said.

Oil firm Petrofina was the biggest gainer with a 4.6 percent rise to 12,550 francs mainly on the dollar, belated fallout from solid earnings and a recent Angolan oil find report by French rival Elf-Aquitaine, analysts said.
KB-Securities analyst Ruth Devenyns said the recent negative bourse climate had smothered the impact of 1996 earnings.
"Now that things are going better again, shares like Petrofina, which fundamentally have something more to offer, will start outperforming," she said.
She said Petrofina also had interests in Angola and could be supported by Elf's major find in the Girassol oil field.
Cyclical stocks in general were the flavour of the day with non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere (UM) adding 4.1 percent to 2,820 francs.
Glass maker Glaverbel rose 3.3 percent to 4,490 and PVC profiles maker Deceuninck gained 2.4 percent at 6,710.
